text:
maya: Heads up — I'm sketching a telemetry bridge for runtime -> console so we can ship the new reliability dashboard.
alex: Nice. Goal is to capture timeouts, 5xx, OOMs, and degraded-mode/fallback counts, right?
maya: Yep. Also some routing/quota labels so product can slice by route/model/customer.
chen: Quick flag — cardinality explosion risk if we tag by full route+model+customer. Need guardrails.
lina: For the dashboard we want per-model and global views. Per-customer is optional behind a sampling flag.
sam: Ops needs the alertable metrics named consistently. Can we propose canonical metric names?
maya: Proposal (draft):
```
redwood.runtime.request_timeout.count
redwood.runtime.5xx.count
redwood.runtime.oom.count
redwood.runtime.fallback.count
redwood.runtime.latency.histogram
redwood.runtime.degraded_mode.active_gauge
```
alex: LGTM for names. Suggest labels: model, deployment, region, route (coarse), customer_id (hashed/sample).
chen: +1 but route should be coarse categorization (eg: /chat, /embed, /rerank) not raw path. Also sample customer_id at 0.1% by default.
lina: For dashboard panels we'll want: error rate (5xx+timeouts) by model, OOM trend, fallback rate by fallback_reason, and % time in degraded_mode.
sam: What's the SLI/alert thresholds? I can wire alerts once we have counts and rate functions.
maya: Draft SLOs: error_rate (5xx+timeout) < 0.5% p95 over 5m; OOM rate < 1 per 10k requests; degraded_mode < 1% of requests per hour.
alex: Can we do error_rate as a ratio: sum(5xx+timeout)/sum(requests) with same label set to avoid mismatch.
chen: Important: store cardinality limits in sidecar. If label cardinality exceeds threshold, drop route label and mark sample.
maya: Implementation options: instrument runtime (fastest), or sidecar exporter that enriches and batches metrics (safer for rollout). Thoughts?
alex: Sidecar allows toggling tag enrichment for Dedicated vs Hosted — useful. Slight latency in emit but fine for dashboards.
chen: Sidecar also lets us cap label sets before pushing to TSDB. I prefer sidecar for initial rollout.
lina: UX note — Console needs a per-route toggle in the rollouts UI to enable expanded metrics. Product can use that to opt-in customers.
sam: Deploy plan: start sidecar in canary region, collect 48h of metrics, validate cardinality and QPS. Then flip for all-hosted.
deploy-bot: deploy started: telemetry-sidecar canary -> region us-west-2 (job 3421)
maya: After canary we'll confirm metric names and labels then Lina will create dashboard JSON and share panels.
lina: I'll prepare dashboards: summary (global), model-slices, fallback-root-causes, OOM drilldown. Will add annotations for canary start.
alex: One more: expose per-route quota usage metric: redwood.quota.route_usage.counter with labels route, customer_tier.
chen: Keep quota usage as a separate endpoint with lower cardinality. No raw customer IDs there.
maya: Action items: maya -> PR with sidecar config & metric names; chen -> add cardinality guard in sidecar; lina -> draft dashboards; sam -> alert rules template.
sam: I'll own runbook updates once alerts are in.
maya: Great. Can everyone ack + add any missing constraints by EOD? We want to kick off canary tomorrow.
alex: Ack.
chen: Ack. I'll add sampling rates and max label counts to the PR.
lina: Ack. I'll attach dashboard JSON to the PR.
sam: Ack. I'll draft alert thresholds and runbook sections.
maya: Thanks all — ping me if anyone needs a schema example. I'm adding a small example payload to the PR.
maya: Example event snippet to wire to sidecar:
```
{ "metric": "redwood.runtime.5xx.count", "labels": {"model":"redwood-1","route":"/chat","region":"us-west-2"}, "value": 1 }
```
alex: Perfect. If we hit cardinality issues, we fallback to aggregated route buckets and hashed customer ids.
chen: Adding: retention policy note — raw high-card metrics only kept 7d, aggregated kept 90d.
maya: Noted. Ok closing the loop — canary tomorrow AM. I'll post final PR link here.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: telemetry-sidecar canary -> us-west-2 (job 3421) :white_check_mark:
maya: Canary looks healthy after 2h. Metrics flowing. Lina, you can start drafting dashboards with real data.
lina: On it, will post first dashboard draft in this thread.
sam: I'll start wiring alerts to staging namespaces.
maya: Thanks everyone."
